title: I did FIFO in the Pilbara as a geologist, so I made a co-op drilling game about it with AI writing the code
author: LittleLimpGames
selftext:
I spent years doing FIFO from Perth to the Pilbara as a geologist and hydrogeologist, and Drilling Down Under is my take on that life. Up to 4 players fly in, run the rig, bag the samples, then lose their pay at the pub. The kangaroos fight back. The Steam page went live today.



I'm not much of a coder, so it's been built almost entirely with Claude Code. I play every build and write up notes (usually screenshots with a lot of red circles on them), and it writes the Unity code, builds it, tests it and uploads it to Steam. We're 53 rounds of notes in.



The bit people don't expect: there are no AI image or 3D generators in the game. The models, from the rigs to the kangaroos to the pub, are built by Python scripts in Blender that the AI writes. The music is from Google's Lyria, off a prompt sheet I wrote. The game even films its own trailer. The camera moves are scripted inside the game, and an automated test runs about 1,466 checks before any build goes up to Steam.



The hard part is that the AI can't see what looks wrong. Tonight's example: the boot you drink a shoey out of looked like a brown cup from first person, and once we fixed that, the hand's thumb was poking out through the leather. Before that it was couches with their backrests facing the wrong way, and a telly that had been built into the pub wall and kept flickering. Spotting that stuff and saying what feels right is basically my whole job now.



Keen to hear from anyone else building their 3D purely from code. How do you handle the things the AI can't see?



Steam store: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5410280/Drilling\_Down\_Under/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5410280/Drilling_Down_Under/)

comments.author: AlgaeNo3373
comments.body:
I see Aussie gamedev I updoot. Not sure I ever seen a more aussie game. Shoeys and miners losing their salary at the pub...lol

Love that you think a bunch of gamedevs know what FIFO is btw :P From screenshots I can see FIFO is literal here, an actual plane in a shot lol. Rather than "The bit people don't expect" maybe go with what they do expect: explanations!   


I think if you're an actual geologist with experience here that should be like, a selling point perhaps? Maybe even a central one? Your steam page doesn't mention it but your reddit post does. I reckon lean into the fact you know LOTS about what you're building here (it's kinda useful when elsewhere you have to disclose the AI).   


Or even just when you say something like "*play-tested by hand"* you can add, playtested and designed by a proffessional geologist with years of experience at both lifting rocks and drinking shoeys blah blah. 

You built a whole game about something you seem to be really knowledgable and passionate about and that seems like a strong selling point to me. Not exactly many FIFO workers vibe coding up games of their experience yknow!

This is the "text copy" version of the AI blindness you talk about btw/imo. If you let it write the copy (which it appears to have) it will also have crazy blind spots like this.

replies.author: LittleLimpGames
replies.body: Thanks! This is some awesome advice! Yeah I think that is the selling point these days when making games. Personal experience needs to come into play more to give unique and interesting experiences. I'll definitely add in your suggestions. Thanks mate 👌
